bills.title: To amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to provide incentives for certain residential rental property.
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 9573 directly implicates IRS and Treasury's Office of Tax Policy, as any amendment to the Internal Revenue Code requires Treasury to develop implementing regulations and guidance. Treasury must assess revenue cost, potential compliance risks, and administrative burden on IRS before the bill advances beyond Ways and Means.

bills.title: Taxpayer Workforce Modernization Act
bills.status: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute by the Yeas and Nays: 24 - 16.
bills.nexus: H.R. 7972 directly implicates IRS workforce authorities under Treasury's oversight, touching hiring flexibilities, compensation structures, and potentially civil service classifications for IRS personnel. The implementation risk centers on Treasury and IRS absorbing new statutory mandates for workforce restructuring while managing ongoing modernization initiatives under the Inflation Reduction Act funding baseline.

bills.title: Tax Exempt Hospital Transparency Act
bills.status: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute by the Yeas and Nays: 25 - 15.
bills.nexus: H.R. 9504 directly implicates the IRS (a Treasury bureau) because it would modify the tax-exempt status requirements and Schedule H reporting obligations governing nonprofit hospitals under Section 501(r) of the Internal Revenue Code. Treasury's implementation risk centers on IRS capacity to process expanded disclosure data and potentially revoke exemptions, raising both administrative burden and revenue baseline concerns.

bills.title: End Tax Penalties on American Hostages Act
bills.status: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute by the Yeas and Nays: 40 - 0.
bills.nexus: H.R. 9496 directly implicates IRS authority under the Internal Revenue Code by requiring the Service to waive tax penalties and interest for Americans wrongfully detained or held hostage abroad during the period of their captivity. Treasury and IRS must assess the administrative mechanics of identifying qualifying individuals, processing penalty abatements, and accounting for any resulting revenue loss, while ensuring the relief framework does not create compliance or fraud vulnerabilities.

bills.title: Taxpayer Advocate Participation Act
bills.status: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute by the Yeas and Nays: 39 - 0.
bills.nexus: H.R. 9498 directly affects the Office of the Taxpayer Advocate (OTA) under IRC Section 7803(c) by expanding taxpayer rights to request Advocate participation during IRS examinations or collection proceedings. Treasury's implementation risk centers on potential resource strain on OTA and the need for regulatory guidance defining the scope and limits of mandated participation.

bills.title: Tax Relief for Fraud Victims Act
bills.status: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute by the Yeas and Nays: 39 - 0.
bills.nexus: H.R. 9500 directly engages IRS authority under the Internal Revenue Code by modifying tax treatment for victims of fraud-related losses, falling within the Office of Tax Policy's purview on casualty and theft loss deduction rules. The unanimous committee vote signals likely floor consideration, requiring IRS to develop administrative guidance and potentially update Form 4684 instructions, creating near-term implementation burden and revenue-scoring obligations for the Joint Committee on Taxation.

bills.title: AI Tax Integrity Act of 2026
bills.status: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute by the Yeas and Nays: 40 - 0.
bills.nexus:
Without a known nexus provided, here is a placeholder briefing based on the bill title alone:

H.R. 9501 would direct IRS (under Treasury's authority over tax administration and enforcement) to develop standards or rules governing AI use in tax compliance and examination processes. Treasury's Office of Tax Policy and IRS would bear primary implementation responsibility, and the bill creates operational and legal risk around how AI-assisted determinations affect taxpayer rights and audit defensibility.

bills.title: Protecting Taxpayers from Ghost Preparers Act
bills.status: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute by the Yeas and Nays: 40 - 0.
bills.nexus: H.R. 9499 directly implicates IRS authority under the Internal Revenue Code to regulate and sanction paid tax return preparers, touching the IRS Return Preparer Office and its enforcement jurisdiction. The implementation risk centers on whether IRS has sufficient statutory authority and resources to identify, penalize, and enjoin "ghost preparers" who prepare returns for compensation without signing them, creating both taxpayer harm and tax gap exposure.

bills.title: Credit Access and Inclusion Act of 2025
bills.status: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 28 - 23.
bills.nexus: H.R. 5402 would amend the Fair Credit Reporting Act to allow reporting of on-time utility, telecom, and rental payment data to consumer reporting agencies, directly implicating Treasury's Office of Consumer Policy and its work on financial inclusion and credit market access. The narrow committee margin (28-23) signals contested implementation questions around data accuracy, consumer harm safeguards, and potential downstream effects on federally supervised lenders and credit markets that Treasury monitors.

bills.title: Community Flood Resilience Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Financial Services.
bills.nexus: H.R. 9056 directly implicates the Federal Insurance Office (FIO) and Treasury's oversight role under the National Flood Insurance Program's fiscal exposure, which sits on the federal balance sheet. Treasury cares because expanded flood resilience mandates or coverage changes could alter federal reinsurance arrangements, shift actuarial risk, and create budget scoring implications requiring interagency coordination with FEMA and OMB.

bills.title: Expressing support for the work of open water lifeguards as first responders and emergency response providers.
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure.
bills.nexus: H.Res. 1188 is a simple House resolution honoring open water lifeguards and does not touch any Treasury office, tax provision, financial regulatory authority, or appropriations stream. Treasury has no implementation role, fiscal exposure, or policy equities in this measure.

bills.title: Big Oil Windfall Profits Tax Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 7960 directly implicates the Internal Revenue Service and the Office of Tax Policy, as it would impose an excise tax on major integrated oil companies' quarterly profits exceeding a pre-pandemic baseline. Treasury bears implementation risk through the need to promulgate regulations defining "windfall profit," establish quarterly reporting mechanisms, and administer refundable consumer rebate credits tied to the new revenue stream.

bills.title: Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026
bills.nexus: H.R. 7148 directly governs discretionary funding levels for the Department of the Treasury, including appropriations for IRS operations, the Office of Financial Research, and Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN). Treasury's implementation risk centers on budget execution across these bureaus, potential continuing-resolution carryover constraints, and maintaining compliance with any new legislative riders or reporting mandates embedded in the act.

bills.title: Helping Young Americans Save for Retirement Act
bills.status: Referred to the Committee on Ways and Means, and in addition to the Committee on Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
bills.nexus: H.R. 4718 directly implicates Treasury's Office of Tax Policy and IRS, as it would amend Internal Revenue Code provisions governing tax-advantaged retirement accounts to allow younger workers, likely those under current age thresholds, to participate in or contribute to qualified plans. Treasury faces implementation risk in issuing conforming regulations and updating IRS plan qualification guidance to reflect any new eligibility rules without disrupting existing plan administration.
